docs.title: Welcome to the Lab Equipment Wiki
docs.text: This wiki provides quick reference guides for all lab equipment. Each page has a corresponding QR code that you can print and attach to the physical equipment.

docs.title: How to Use This Wiki
docs.text:
1. Find your equipment in the navigation menu
  2. Read the guide for basic usage instructions
  3. Download the QR code from the QR Codes page
  4. Print and attach the QR code sticker to the equipment

New Members

If you're new to the lab, start with the General Lab Safety guide.

docs.title: Before You Start
docs.text: Always start with the meter in the OFF position or highest range to prevent damage.

docs.title: DC Voltage (V with straight line)
docs.text:
1. Set dial to DC voltage position
  2. Red probe to VΩ jack, black probe to COM jack
  3. Touch probes to circuit in parallel

docs.title: AC Voltage (V with wavy line)
docs.text:
1. Set dial to AC voltage position
  2. Same probe configuration as DC
  3. Useful for mains voltage measurements

High Voltage Warning

Never measure voltages above the meter's rating (typically 600V or 1000V)

docs.title: DC Current (A with straight line)
docs.text:
1. IMPORTANT: Must break the circuit and measure in series
  2. For currents < 200mA: Red probe to mA jack
  3. For currents > 200mA: Red probe to 10A jack
  4. Set dial to appropriate DC current range

Fuse Protection

The mA jack is fuse-protected. If you measure high current through this jack, you'll blow the fuse. Always use the 10A jack if unsure.

docs.title: Measuring Resistance (Ω)
docs.text:
1. Power off the circuit first!
  2. Set dial to Ω position
  3. Red probe to VΩ jack, black probe to COM
  4. Touch probes to component

docs.title: Continuity Testing (beeper symbol)
docs.text:
1. Set dial to continuity mode (usually shows a sound wave or speaker symbol)
  2. Touch probes together - should beep
  3. Use to check connections, find shorts, or verify conductors

docs.title: Diode Testing (diode symbol)
docs.text:
1. Set dial to diode mode
  2. Red probe to anode, black to cathode
  3. Should show forward voltage drop (~0.6V for silicon)
  4. Reverse probes - should show OL (open)

docs.title: Safety
docs.text:
• Never measure resistance or continuity on powered circuits
  • Start with highest range and work down
  • Watch for the 10A jack time limit (usually 10 seconds max)
  • Replace blown fuses immediately - don't operate without them

docs.title: Testing a Battery
docs.text:
1. Set to DC voltage
  2. Touch probes to battery terminals
  3. Compare reading to rated voltage

docs.title: Testing a Fuse
docs.text:
1. Power off circuit
  2. Remove fuse
  3. Set to continuity mode
  4. Touch probes to both ends - should beep if good

docs.title: Finding a Short Circuit
docs.text:
1. Power off circuit
  2. Set to continuity mode
  3. Test between suspected shorted points
  4. Beep indicates a short (unwanted connection)

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text: Problem Solution Display shows "OL" or "1" Out of range - select higher range No reading at all Check battery, check probe connections Erratic readings Clean probe tips, check for loose connections Won't measure current Check if fuse is blown

docs.title: Maintenance
docs.text:
• Replace battery when low battery indicator appears
  • Keep probes clean - wipe with isopropyl alcohol
  • Store in case when not in use
  • Check calibration annually for precision work
  • Keep spare fuses on hand

docs.title: Basic Setup
docs.text:
1. Power On: Press the power button on the front panel
  2. Connect Probe: Attach the probe to Channel 1 (yellow input)
  3. Ground Reference: Connect the probe's ground clip to your circuit's ground

docs.title: Vertical Controls (Y-Axis)
docs.text:
• Volts/Div: Adjusts the vertical scale (voltage per division)
  • Position: Moves the trace up or down on the screen
  • Coupling: Set to DC for most measurements, AC to remove DC offset

docs.title: Horizontal Controls (X-Axis)
docs.text:
• Time/Div: Adjusts the horizontal scale (time per division)
  • Position: Shifts the trace left or right

docs.title: Trigger Controls
docs.text:
• Level: Sets the voltage level where the scope starts capturing
  • Source: Select which channel triggers the capture
  • Slope: Rising edge (/) or falling edge () trigger

docs.title: Measuring Voltage
docs.text:
1. Adjust Volts/Div so the signal fills about 60-80% of the screen
  2. Count the vertical divisions peak-to-peak
  3. Multiply by Volts/Div setting

docs.title: Measuring Frequency
docs.text:
1. Adjust Time/Div to show 1-2 complete cycles
  2. Measure the time for one complete cycle (period)
  3. Frequency = 1 / Period

docs.title: Safety Tips
docs.text:
Safety First

  • Never exceed the maximum input voltage (typically 300V)
  • Always connect the ground clip first
  • Use appropriate probe attenuation (10X for most signals)
  • Be careful with mains voltage - use isolated probes if needed

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text: Problem Solution No signal visible Check trigger level, adjust time/div, verify connections Signal too noisy Enable bandwidth limiting, check ground connections Unstable display Adjust trigger level and slope

docs.title: Need Help?
docs.text: Contact the lab manager or check the manufacturer's manual (stored in the drawer below the scope).

docs.title: Setup
docs.text:
1. Power on the station
  2. Set temperature: 350°C (660°F) for standard lead-free solder
  3. Wait for ready indicator (usually a green light)
  4. Tin the tip: Melt a small amount of solder on the tip before first use

docs.title: Basic Soldering Technique
docs.text:
1. Clean surfaces: Both surfaces should be clean and oxide-free
  2. Heat both parts: Touch the iron to both the pad and component lead
  3. Apply solder: Feed solder into the joint (not onto the iron)
  4. Remove solder, then iron: Let it cool naturally
  5. Inspect joint: Should be shiny, smooth, and volcano-shaped

docs.title: Good vs Bad Joints
docs.text: Good Joint Bad Joint Shiny, smooth Dull, grainy (cold joint) Volcano shape Ball shape (insufficient heating) Solder flows onto surfaces Solder blobs on top

docs.title: Temperature Guide
docs.text: Solder Type Temperature Lead-free (SAC305) 350-380°C Leaded (60/40) 300-330°C SMD components 320-350°C

docs.title: Tip Maintenance
docs.text:
• Clean frequently: Use brass sponge after every few joints
  • Re-tin regularly: Keep the tip coated with fresh solder
  • Never file tips: This removes the protective plating
  • Replace when worn: Black, pitted tips need replacement

docs.title: Safety
docs.text:
Burn Hazard

The tip reaches 350°C+ and stays hot for several minutes after power-off.

  • Always return iron to holder
  • Never touch tip or nearby metal
  • Solder in ventilated area - fumes are harmful
  • Wear safety glasses
  • Tie back long hair
  • No loose clothing or jewelry

docs.title: Cleanup
docs.text:
1. Power off station
  2. Let cool completely (15+ minutes)
  3. Store tips properly
  4. Wipe down work area
  5. Dispose of solder scraps in designated container
